title: Light Syrian Lamb Tagine
description: A traditional Syrian dish made with lamb, fermented ingredients, and a blend of sugars, cooked in a tandoor clay pot with beurre monte, perfect for a sick day, this low calorie friendly recipe is sure to delight.
instructions: Preheat the tandoor clay pot to 300 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large bowl, whisk together the sumac, cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper.
Add the lamb pieces to the bowl and toss to coat with the spice mixture.
Heat the beurre monte in the preheated tandoor clay pot over medium heat.
Add the lamb pieces to the pot and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the fermented turnips, date syrup, and pomegranate molasses to the pot, stirring to combine.
Cover the pot and transfer to the oven, cooking for 2 hours, or until the lamb is tender.
Remove the pot from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve the tagine hot, garnished with fresh parsley and a dollop of yogurt, if desired.
